Diabetes mellitus is a chronic metabolic condition characterized by elevated levels of blood glucose (sugar), which leads over time to serious damage to the heart, blood vessels, eyes, kidneys, and nerves.
Diabetes occurs when your pancreas does not produce enough insulin, or when the body cannot effectively use the insulin it produces. Insulin is a hormone that regulates blood glucose.

patterns: what are the symptoms of diabetes
how do I know if I have diabetes
responses: Common symptoms of diabetes include: 1) Increased thirst (polydipsia), 2) Frequent urination (polyuria), 3) Increased hunger (polyphagia), 4) Unexplained weight loss, 5) Fatigue and blurred vision, and 6) Slow-healing sores. Please consult a doctor for clinical testing.

Diabetes risk factors include genetic predisposition (family history), obesity/high BMI, physical inactivity, unhealthy diet, age, and high blood pressure. Type 1 is an autoimmune condition, while Type 2 is largely linked to metabolic and lifestyle factors.

patterns: how to avoid high sugar levels
responses: Type 2 diabetes can often be prevented or delayed through healthy lifestyle choices: 1) Maintain a healthy body weight, 2) Stay physically active (150 mins/week), 3) Eat a balanced diet low in refined sugars and saturated fats, and 4) Avoid tobacco use.

patterns: what is a healthy diabetes diet
what foods to eat for diabetes
what to avoid eating for sugar
responses: A diabetes-friendly diet emphasizes whole grains, leafy green vegetables, lean proteins, high-fiber foods, and healthy fats while limiting refined carbohydrates, sugary beverages, processed snacks, and excessive sodium.

patterns: is physical activity good for sugar
how much exercise do I need
responses: Regular exercise helps increase insulin sensitivity so your body can better utilize available glucose. Aim for at least 30 minutes of moderate aerobic activity (brisk walking, cycling, swimming) 5 days a week, combined with light resistance training.

Body Mass Index (BMI) measures body fat based on height and weight. Normal BMI ranges from 18.5 to 24.9. A BMI above 25 is considered overweight, and above 30 indicates obesity, which significantly increases diabetes risk.

Key habits for a healthy lifestyle include maintaining a nutrient-dense diet, staying active daily, getting 7-8 hours of quality sleep, managing stress levels, staying hydrated, and undergoing regular routine health checkups.
